No file picker is available on this phone. Install a file manager or use Share from another app.

If Android will not let you allow SMS (Android 13 and newer, app installed outside a store):
1. Open Settings › Apps › GeekBridge (the button above).
2. Tap the ⋮ menu at the top right › Allow restricted settings, and confirm with your screen lock.
3. Come back, switch on Messages and tap Allow for SMS (or Settings › Apps › GeekBridge › Permissions › SMS › Allow).

GeekBridge does not need to be your default SMS app and never asks to be. It reads the SMS store and sends plain texts. Picture messages (MMS) and RCS chats stay in your messaging app, and marking a message read on the computer does not mark it read on the phone.
All set. You can change this later in app settings.

Paired computers you allow “Calls” for see ringing and in-call, and can answer, decline or end. Off by default.

Call audio does not travel through GeekBridge. It stays on the phone unless your computer is also paired with this phone over Bluetooth as a hands-free device. Needs the Phone state step; declining and ending a call needs Android 9 or newer.
Tap below and choose “Allow”. GeekBridge uses almost no power while idle; this only stops Android from pausing it.
Background use is restricted for GeekBridge. In app settings open Battery and choose “Unrestricted” (or “Allow background usage”).
Android will not pause GeekBridge to save battery.

resources.string: Pair this phone with your computer once. After that they find each other on your network automatically, and nothing is trusted until you confirm a matching code.
Lets GeekBridge show a quiet notice while it stays connected, and tell you about incoming files.
Lets this phone show names instead of numbers for calls and messages, and, if you share contacts, fills the Contacts app on your computer. Read on this phone; nothing is uploaded.

Lets you share your calendars (including Google Calendar accounts that sync on this phone) with the Calendar app on your computer. Read-only; the computer can only add or change events if you separately switch on editing later, in Share with computer.
Lets GeekBridge know whether the phone is idle, ringing or in a call. It never sees phone numbers or call history.

Lets a paired computer you trust answer, decline or end a call on this phone, so a ringing call can be handled from your desk. GeekBridge cannot hear the call: audio stays on the phone unless the computer is also its Bluetooth hands-free device.

Android only gives an app the caller\'s number if it can read the call log. Allow this to show who is calling on your computer; with your contacts allowed it also shows the name. Without it the computer shows “Unknown caller”. Read on this phone only; the call log is never read or sent.

Optionally share your contacts, calendar and text messages with a paired computer. Everything is off until you switch it on here, and each part needs its own Android permission. Text messages are limited by Android and Google Play; the notes below explain how.
Keeps the connection to your computer alive when the screen is off. Without this, Android may pause GeekBridge and files or clipboard may arrive late.
Open GeekBridge or KDE Connect on your computer, on the same Wi-Fi network as this phone, then look for it.
To unpair a computer, go to Home > Diagnostics & about > Unpair.
To add another computer, open GeekBridge on it, on the same Wi-Fi network, then look for it.
Looking for computers on this network… keep GeekBridge open on the computer. Nothing showing up? Check that both devices use the same Wi-Fi and that a guest or VPN network is not in the way.
